Biology is pivotal in forestry, aiding our understanding and management of forests and wildlife. Forest ecology delves into how organisms interact with their environment, crucial for wildlife habitats. Recognizing floral diversity is key for preserving plant species vital for wildlife. Microbiology uncovers how microorganisms support soil health, benefiting both forests and wildlife. Conservation biology ensures sustainable practices, safeguarding wildlife habitats within forests. These biology scopes empower foresters to protect forests and wildlife, benefiting ecosystems and human communities alike.
